title: Customer-story content package
scope: One short owner interview, three captions based on it, and a shot list using the business’s real work. One revision round. Filming is a separately priced option.
buyers: Owner-led salons, gyms, cafés, and local service businesses.
signals: An active account showing real work, but little explanation of the process or customer experience. Confirm that content support is a priority before pitching.
search: Search a business category and city. Review the account, linked website, and recent posts to check fit.
demo: Show how an owner’s real explanation becomes a useful post. Use your own sample or get permission for client material.
competition: Other content providers and AI writing tools.
reason: AI can draft captions. Interviewing, verifying details, and capturing the owner’s real perspective provide the distinction.
strength: Sell original source material, accuracy, and a finished package rather than a quantity of generic captions.
test: Ask one suitable owner whether turning their real process into three useful posts would help. Offer the defined paid pilot.
priceBasis: No like-for-like price comparison verified. Get local or niche quotes and test buyer willingness to pay before setting a price.

title: Small product-photo session
scope: Five edited product photos, one product, one simple setting, and one revision round. Client provides the product; exclude studio rental and extensive retouching.
buyers: Small makers, bakeries, and independent product brands.
signals: Products are for sale and regularly posted, but useful angles, scale, or consistent lighting are missing.
search: Search a product category plus your city or a maker market. Check that the seller has an active offer.
demo: Photograph an item you own with three useful angles. Show the lighting and final image.
competition: Photographers, DIY phone photography, and AI image tools.
reason: Real product handling and accurate details help differentiate this from generated scenes. Editing still competes with automated tools.
strength: Emphasize accurate real-product images, consistent lighting, and usable files. Never misrepresent product details.
test: Show a relevant sample to one nearby seller and ask whether they need accurate images of a specific product.
priceBasis: No like-for-like price comparison verified. Get local or niche quotes and test buyer willingness to pay before setting a price.

title: One-space organization session
scope: One three-hour session for one small closet or workspace. Client purchases storage supplies separately. Exclude hauling, hazardous material, and whole-home work.
buyers: Local residents or small studio owners wanting practical organization.
signals: Look for explicit requests, local introductions, or relevant community conversations. Do not assume a need from someone’s home photos.
search: Use local neighborhood and professional accounts to find appropriate introductions and permitted community requests.
demo: Show a space you own before and after, plus one organizing principle. Get permission before sharing another person’s space.
competition: Local organizers and DIY advice; AI tools can provide instructions.
reason: The paid deliverable is physical work, tailored decisions, and execution in the space.
strength: A clear boundary, respectful handling, and a finished usable space.
test: Offer a narrowly scoped session to someone who has expressed a need; confirm access, safety, and expectations first.
priceBasis: No like-for-like price comparison verified. Get local or niche quotes and test buyer willingness to pay before setting a price.

title: Simple garment-repair pilot
scope: Up to three straightforward repairs such as buttons or open seams, after inspecting the garments. Exclude complex fit alterations, specialty fabrics, and items outside your experience.
buyers: Local customers, vintage sellers, or small resale businesses.
signals: An explicit repair request or a resale seller discussing repairable inventory. Confirm the material and job before quoting.
search: Search your city with vintage, resale, or sewing. Look for collaboration needs, rather than unsolicited comments on clothing.
demo: Show a repair on your own garment with close-ups of the finish.
competition: Alteration shops, repair providers, and customer DIY.
reason: AI can explain a repair, but the customer still needs someone to perform the physical work competently.
strength: Reliable inspection, honest limits, quality finishing, and clear turnaround.
test: Inspect one small job and quote a paid repair with a written scope.
priceBasis: No like-for-like price comparison verified. Get local or niche quotes and test buyer willingness to pay before setting a price.

title: One practical skill lesson
scope: One 45-minute lesson, preparation, and a one-page practice guide for one narrow skill you can teach competently. No ongoing support included.
buyers: Beginners already discussing a specific task in your area of expertise.
signals: Questions about a concrete task or repeated difficulty. For fitness, stay within your qualifications; exclude medical or rehabilitation advice.
search: Search the task or hobby, then examine genuine beginner questions and relevant account communities. Follow community rules.
demo: Teach one small step using your own demonstration, then show what a full lesson helps someone practice.
competition: Teachers, free tutorials, courses, and AI tutors.
reason: Generic explanations are easy to replace. Live observation, tailored feedback, and guided practice provide the distinction.
strength: A specific task and feedback on the learner’s own work.
test: Ask one interested beginner if they want a paid guided session for a clearly defined task.
priceBasis: No like-for-like price comparison verified. Get local or niche quotes and test buyer willingness to pay before setting a price.

title: Inventory-tracker setup
scope: One simple tracker, import of up to 50 clean items, and a 30-minute handover. No accounting, custom integrations, or ongoing maintenance.
buyers: Small makers and resale sellers managing a modest catalog.
signals: The owner describes stock-tracking problems or asks about organizing inventory. A busy feed alone does not prove the need.
search: Search small maker and resale categories. Look for stated operational problems and ask how inventory is currently tracked.
demo: Use fictional data to show stock in, stock out, and low-stock review. Keep customer data private.
competition: Spreadsheet specialists, inventory software, templates, and AI-generated formulas.
reason: AI can build a generic sheet. Understanding the workflow, cleaning real data, and teaching the owner to use it add value.
strength: Setup and handover that fit the owner’s process, with a small defined scope.
test: Ask a suitable seller about their current tracking process. Demonstrate a sample before proposing the paid setup.
priceBasis: Scope estimate: four hours × Upwork’s published $12–$30/hour Excel-expert range. This is a derived project estimate, not an observed fixed-price listing. Confirm your actual time and expenses.

title: Product-to-Pinterest starter package
scope: Five static Pin designs and matching titles for five existing product or useful resource pages. Client provides assets. No account management or traffic promise.
buyers: Visual product businesses with functioning destination pages.
signals: An active Instagram shop or portfolio, clear products, and an owner interested in reaching people outside Instagram.
search: Find visual product accounts in one niche. Check their website and whether each proposed Pin has a useful destination.
demo: Show one original product-to-Pin transformation and explain the destination and intended audience.
competition: Designers, template tools, AI design, and DIY Pinterest work.
reason: Generic layouts and text are readily automated. Product-specific decisions and working destination mapping improve the offer but do not remove competition.
strength: Accurate product assets, clear messaging, and a relevant destination for every Pin.
test: Ask whether the owner wants a small Pinterest content test. Sell the deliverables, not promised reach.
priceBasis: No like-for-like price comparison verified. Get local or niche quotes and test buyer willingness to pay before setting a price.

title: One original beginner pattern
scope: One original, tested pattern for a simple project, with measurements, materials, photos, and beginner instructions. Do not use other creators’ patterns without permission. Use materials and tools you already own for the sample; if new materials are necessary, include them in your budget.
buyers: Beginners who want to make that particular project.
signals: Questions about making the item, requests for instructions, or responses to your own finished-project demonstrations.
search: Search the project and beginner hobby community. Learn what people struggle with and follow sharing rules.
demo: Show the finished project, one construction step, and the materials needed.
competition: Pattern designers, free tutorials, and AI-generated instructions.
reason: Text is easy to generate. A real finished sample, tested dimensions, and clear photos distinguish the resource.
strength: A tested project with evidence of fit or construction and useful beginner detail.
test: Share your original project and ask whether people want the tested instructions. Build a small paid version after learning their needs.
priceBasis: Suggested beginner price test, not an observed sales range. Established Closet Core garment PDF patterns list at $18; a simpler first pattern may justify less. Complexity, testing, sizing, and instructions matter.

title: Small personalized handmade item
scope: One simple item you can reliably make, with one personalization option. Price shipping separately. Exclude complex customization until you measure production time.
buyers: People looking for a specific gift or useful item within your niche.
signals: Explicit gift requests, customization questions, or interest in your own sample. Confirm occasion and delivery timing.
search: Search the item and occasion. Use your own content and relevant maker communities to invite inquiries without spamming.
demo: Show the making process, finished details, scale, and personalization options.
competition: Makers, mass-produced alternatives, and print-on-demand sellers.
reason: AI may help with design, but physical production and finishing remain part of the value. Other sellers can still offer close substitutes.
strength: Distinct materials, reliable workmanship, and a small repeatable customization process.
test: Make one sample, calculate real costs, and offer a limited paid batch you can fulfill on time.
priceBasis: No like-for-like price comparison verified. Get local or niche quotes and test buyer willingness to pay before setting a price.

title: Maker order-tracker template
scope: One original spreadsheet for small makers to track customer orders, due dates, and fulfillment, plus a worked example and setup guide. Exclude accounting and integrations.
buyers: Small handmade sellers who manage custom orders themselves.
signals: Questions about managing custom orders, missed deadlines, or tracking fulfillment. Ask about the actual workflow before assuming a spreadsheet solves it.
search: Search handmade and custom-order categories. Read genuine seller questions and join relevant discussions where participation is welcome.
demo: Show a fictional order from inquiry through completion. Demonstrate one useful view and make the setup clear.
competition: Free templates, software, spreadsheet creators, and AI tools.
reason: AI can produce a basic tracker. A generic spreadsheet has substantial competition; a narrowly tested workflow and clear tutorial are essential.
strength: Test it with a specific maker workflow, include realistic sample data, and document its limits.
test: Show a working sample to three makers. Ask what they currently use and test whether anyone will pay for the narrow version.
priceBasis: No like-for-like price comparison verified. Get local or niche quotes and test buyer willingness to pay before setting a price.

title: Beginner garment-repair photo guide
scope: An original photographed guide to three simple repairs you can competently demonstrate, using garments and materials you already own. Include tools, steps, mistakes, and clear limits.
buyers: Beginners interested in maintaining or repairing their own clothing.
signals: Specific questions about a repair or requests for steps after your own repair demonstration.
search: Search visible-mending, sewing-beginner, and clothing-care topics. Identify real questions and follow community rules.
demo: Show your own garment before, during, and after a repair. Let people inspect the finish.
competition: Free tutorials, repair guides, creators, and AI-generated instructions.
reason: Generic written instructions are easy to automate. Your original close-up photos, tested steps, and troubleshooting provide more value.
strength: Choose a narrow repair problem and demonstrate the steps clearly on real fabric.
test: Publish one useful repair demonstration, invite interested beginners to view a paid-guide preview, and record actual purchase interest.
priceBasis: No like-for-like price comparison verified. Get local or niche quotes and test buyer willingness to pay before setting a price.

title: Tested small workshop-project plan
scope: One original nonstructural storage project you have actually built: measurements, cut list, materials, photos, and assembly steps. Existing tools and sample materials assumed. Exclude safety-critical jigs and structural designs.
buyers: Hobby woodworkers with a specific storage problem.
signals: A specific question, request, or stated problem related to this offer. Ask about their existing solution and whether they want help; an active account is not proof of demand.
search: Search small-shop organization and woodworking project topics. Look for questions about dimensions and construction.
demo: Show your own completed build, measurements, and one construction step.
competition: Other specialist providers, free resources, DIY tools, and AI-assisted alternatives.
reason: AI can generate plans, but physical testing and accurate dimensions provide a distinction.
strength: A build you have verified, clear photos, and documented limits.
test: Show the real project and test interest in a paid set of instructions.
priceBasis: Suggested price test informed by WOOD Store’s individual project-plan asking prices around $5.95–$14.95. These are comparisons, not proven sales or a guarantee your plan can command them.

title: Niche workout-log spreadsheet
scope: One tested workout-recording template with sample data and instructions. Log sets, reps, and personal notes; exclude exercise prescriptions and health advice.
buyers: People tracking a specific type of training.
signals: A specific question, request, or stated problem related to this offer. Ask about their existing solution and whether they want help; an active account is not proof of demand.
search: Search the training niche and workout-log discussions. Ask what people currently record and what is missing.
demo: Show fictional training entries and a useful progress view, without claiming health results.
competition: Other specialist providers, free resources, DIY tools, and AI-assisted alternatives.
reason: Simple trackers are easy to create with AI and compete with inexpensive downloads and free apps.
strength: A genuinely useful niche workflow and tested usability, rather than decorative charts.
test: Share a sample view and ask interested users whether they would pay for the tested version.
priceBasis: Suggested test range; one comparable workout spreadsheet lists at $3.28, while other marketplace listings vary. This limited sample does not establish a market-wide range.

title: Vehicle-service record template
scope: One spreadsheet for dates, mileage, receipts, and service notes, plus sample data. Users supply their manufacturer service schedule; do not invent maintenance intervals.
buyers: Car enthusiasts documenting a project or owners tracking more than one vehicle.
signals: A specific question, request, or stated problem related to this offer. Ask about their existing solution and whether they want help; an active account is not proof of demand.
search: Search project-car and vehicle-record discussions. Look for explicit recordkeeping problems.
demo: Demonstrate a fictional vehicle’s service history and receipt index.
competition: Other specialist providers, free resources, DIY tools, and AI-assisted alternatives.
reason: Generic logs are easy to automate and compete with apps and free templates.
strength: A specific recordkeeping workflow, clear instructions, and user-provided schedules.
test: Test a sample with three people who actually keep vehicle records before making a paid version.
priceBasis: No like-for-like price comparison verified. Define the scope, check comparable offers, and test willingness to pay.

title: Three short-video edits
scope: Edit three clips up to 30 seconds each from supplied footage: simple cuts, checked captions, and one revision. Exclude filming, advanced effects, and music licensing.
buyers: Coaches, hobby creators, detailers, tradespeople, and outdoor businesses.
signals: A specific question, request, or stated problem related to this offer. Ask about their existing solution and whether they want help; an active account is not proof of demand.
search: Search one niche for accounts publishing real footage. Ask whether editing time is an actual problem.
demo: Edit your own sample footage and show raw versus finished clips.
competition: Other specialist providers, free resources, DIY tools, and AI-assisted alternatives.
reason: Automatic clipping and captions compete directly; editorial judgment and verified niche details add value.
strength: Good selection, pacing, accurate captions, and reliable delivery using the client’s real material.
test: Offer one small paid edit package with approved source footage.
priceBasis: Derived project estimate: three hours × Upwork’s published $10–$60/hour video-editor range. It is broad and not a fixed-package market rate.

title: Job-tracking spreadsheet setup
scope: One simple job tracker with status, due date, customer reference, and up to 50 clean entries. Include handover; exclude accounting, integrations, and sensitive payment data.
buyers: Detailers, repair shops, and small trade businesses.
signals: A specific question, request, or stated problem related to this offer. Ask about their existing solution and whether they want help; an active account is not proof of demand.
search: Search a trade and location. Ask how jobs and follow-ups are tracked before suggesting a tool.
demo: Show fictional jobs moving from inquiry to scheduled to complete.
competition: Other specialist providers, free resources, DIY tools, and AI-assisted alternatives.
reason: AI can generate a tracker; workflow discovery, setup, and teaching the owner provide more value.
strength: A simple system that fits actual work and gets used.
test: Demonstrate one realistic workflow and quote a scoped setup.
priceBasis: Derived estimate using four hours and Upwork’s published $12–$30/hour Excel-expert range; verify real project requirements.

title: Website purchase-path check
scope: Manually check five pages on phone and desktop; report ten prioritized problems with screenshots and reproduction steps. No legal accessibility certification, security audit, or repairs included.
buyers: Small businesses with an active website and Instagram presence.
signals: A specific question, request, or stated problem related to this offer. Ask about their existing solution and whether they want help; an active account is not proof of demand.
search: Review the linked website of a suitable business. Mention a specific observable issue and ask whether a scoped check would help.
demo: Use a demonstration site to show one broken handoff and a clear issue report.
competition: Other specialist providers, free resources, DIY tools, and AI-assisted alternatives.
reason: Automated tools identify many errors; testing real user journeys and verifying findings are the distinction.
strength: Reproducible issues, screenshots, clear prioritization, and honest limits.
test: Show one verified issue privately, then offer the defined paid review.
priceBasis: No like-for-like price comparison verified. Define the scope, check comparable offers, and test willingness to pay.

title: Task-specific software tutorial pack
scope: Three original screen-recorded tutorials and a quick reference for one narrow workflow you have verified. State the tested software version. No employer data or unlicensed assets.
buyers: Beginners using a specific tool for a specific task.
signals: A specific question, request, or stated problem related to this offer. Ask about their existing solution and whether they want help; an active account is not proof of demand.
search: Find software communities and creators receiving repeated workflow questions. Respect community promotion rules.
demo: Show one completed task and a short portion of your actual demonstration.
competition: Other specialist providers, free resources, DIY tools, and AI-assisted alternatives.
reason: AI assistants and free tutorials can explain common tasks. Verified demonstrations and a very specific workflow provide distinction.
strength: Current, tested steps with realistic troubleshooting and a clear outcome.
test: Teach one useful step freely and test interest in the focused tutorial pack.
priceBasis: No like-for-like price comparison verified. Define the scope, check comparable offers, and test willingness to pay.

title: Tested gear-care mini guide
scope: An original illustrated guide to cleaning and organizing one type of non-safety-critical gear you know well. Exclude repairs to protective equipment, brakes, electrical systems, or other safety-critical parts.
buyers: People maintaining equipment in your hobby niche.
signals: A specific question, request, or stated problem related to this offer. Ask about their existing solution and whether they want help; an active account is not proof of demand.
search: Search the exact gear type and care questions; ask what users find difficult.
demo: Show your own real process and a useful before-and-after.
competition: Other specialist providers, free resources, DIY tools, and AI-assisted alternatives.
reason: Generic advice is easily generated; original photos, tested steps, and precise limitations add value.
strength: A narrow, verified task and transparent limits.
test: Publish one useful demonstration and test demand for the fuller guide.
priceBasis: No like-for-like price comparison verified. Define the scope, check comparable offers, and test willingness to pay.
